To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the NBO approach is an efficient method for the analysis of paramagnetic relaxation and chemical shift tensors in metalloprotes, and that it is a useful method to derive structural information about metal sites from NMR parameters.

the natural bond orbital approach allows a fast and accurate calculation of paramagnetic nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) parameters and that these parameters can be used to derive geometric restraints for the structure determination of paramagnetic metalloproteinas in solution.

the NBO approach is a powerful method for the analysis of unpaired spin density in paramagnetic metalloprotein systems, and allows an accurate description and prediction of paramagnetic Nuclei Magnetic Resonance parameters, including paramagnetic relaxation enhancement rates and 15N chemical shift anisotropies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computational method for a fast and reliable calculation of NMR parameters of paramagnetic proteins.
the structure and dynamics of the metal site in metalloprotein.
the accurate calculation of NMR parameters of metalloprotenins, which are used as restraints in molecular dynamics and structure determination protocols.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NBOs are a useful tool in describing paramagnetic NMR effects in metalloprotein systems.
this work provides a very promising approach for the structure determination of metalloprotenins from NMR parameters.
this work is a nice example of how NBO analysis can provide a deeper understanding of the nature of chemical bonding, in particular for paramagnetic species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NBO approach provides a fast and robust method to calculate paramagnetic NMR properties of metallopro- teins and to include them in a structure optimization procedure.
the NBO approach provides a fast and reliable method to calculate the paramagnetic NMR relaxation of nuclei in metallopro- teins and to determine their geometric structure.
the NBO approach can be used for the calculation of paramagnetic relaxation rates and the Fermi-contact shift for protons and the paramagnetic relaxation rates for 15N nuclei.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a paramagnetic relaxation enhancement of 15N can serve as a reliable geometric restraint for structure determination of paramagnetic metalloproteinas.

a small subset of NBOs, which reflect the chemical bonding situation at the metal-site, can be used to describe the paramagnetic NMR properties of a large variety of paramagnetic metalloproteines, including the geometric structure of the metal-site.
the unpaired electron density in metalloprotein structures can be modeled accurately by only a few localized NBOs, which reflect the bonding environment of the metal-site.
